cases.sentence: Для женитьбы нужно было согласие отца, и для этого на ___ князь Андрей уехал к отцу.
cases.explain: «другой день» — after the preposition «на», the accusative marks the direct object of the verb.
cases.translation: Prince Andréy needed his father’s consent to his marriage, and to obtain this he started for the country next day.

cases.sentence: Отец с ___, но внутреннею злобой принял сообщение сына.
cases.explain: «наружным спокойствием» — after the preposition «с», the instrumental marks the means, company, or complement.
cases.translation: His father received his son’s communication with external composure, but inward wrath. He could not comprehend how anyone could wish to alter his life or introduce anything new into it, when his own life was already ending. “If only they would let me end my days as I want to,” thought the old man, “then they might do as they please.” With his son, however, he employed the diplomacy he reserved for important occasions and, adopting a quiet tone, discussed the whole matter.

cases.sentence: С сыном однако он употребил ту дипломацию, которую он употреблял в ___.
cases.explain: «важных случаях» — after the preposition «в», for location or topic.

cases.sentence: Через три недели после своего ___ у Ростовых, князь Андрей вернулся в Петербург.
cases.explain: «последнего вечера» — after the preposition «после», the genitive here marks possession, absence, or quantity.
cases.translation: Three weeks after the last evening he had spent with the Rostóvs, Prince Andréy returned to Petersburg.

cases.sentence: Она, напившись чаю, пошла в залу, которую она особенно любила за ___, и начала петь свои солфеджи (упражнения пения).
cases.explain: «сильный резонанс» — after the preposition «за», the accusative marks the direct object of the verb.
cases.translation: The day after this conversation Natásha put on the old dress which she knew had the peculiar property of conducing to cheerfulness in the mornings, and that day she returned to the old way of life which she had abandoned since the ball. Having finished her morning tea she went to the ballroom, which she particularly liked for its loud resonance, and began singing her solfeggio. When she had finished her first exercise she stood still in the middle of the room and sang a musical phrase that particularly pleased her. She listened joyfully (as though she had not expected it) to the charm of the notes reverberating, filling the whole empty ballroom, and slowly dying away; and all at once she felt cheerful. “What’s the good of making so much of it? Things are nice as it is,” she said to herself, and she began walking up and down the room, not stepping simply on the resounding parquet but treading with each step from the heel to the toe (she had on a new and favorite pair of shoes) and listening to the regular tap of the heel and creak of the toe as gladly as she had to the sounds of her own voice. Passing a mirror she glanced into it. “There, that’s me!” the expression of her face seemed to say as she caught sight of herself. “Well, and very nice too! I need nobody.”

cases.sentence: Окончив ___, она остановилась на середине залы и повторила одну музыкальную фразу, особенно понравившуюся ей.
cases.explain: «первый урок» — the accusative marks the direct object of the verb.

cases.sentence: Она возвратилась в это утро опять к своему ___ любви к себе и восхищения перед собою.
cases.explain: «любимому состоянию» — after the preposition «к», the dative marks the indirect object or recipient.
cases.translation: A footman wanted to come in to clear away something in the room but she would not let him, and having closed the door behind him continued her walk. That morning she had returned to her favorite mood—love of, and delight in, herself. “How charming that Natásha is!” she said again, speaking as some third, collective, male person. “Pretty, a good voice, young, and in nobody’s way if only they leave her in peace.” But however much they left her in peace she could not now be at peace, and immediately felt this. In the hall the porch door opened, and someone asked, “At home?” and then footsteps were heard. Natásha was looking at the mirror, but did not see herself. She listened to the sounds in the hall. When she saw herself, her face was pale. It was he. She knew this for certain, though she hardly heard his voice through the closed doors.

cases.sentence: — Я не был у вас всё это время, потому что был у отца: мне нужно было переговорить с ним о весьма ___.
cases.explain: «важном деле» — after the preposition «о», for location or topic.
cases.translation: “I have not been to see you all this time because I have been at my father’s. I had to talk over a very important matter with him. I only got back last night,” he said glancing at Natásha; “I want to have a talk with you, Countess,” he added after a moment’s pause.

cases.sentence: — Мне нужно переговорить с вами, графиня, — прибавил он после ___.
cases.explain: «минутного молчания» — after the preposition «после», the genitive here marks possession, absence, or quantity.
cases.translation: “I have not been to see you all this time because I have been at my father’s. I had to talk over a very important matter with him. I only got back last night,” he said glancing at Natásha; “I want to have a talk with you, Countess,” he added after a moment’s pause.

cases.sentence: Наташа знала, что ей надо уйти, но она не могла этого сделать: что-то сжимало ей горло, и она неучтиво, прямо, ___ смотрела на князя Андрея.
cases.explain: «открытыми глазами» — the instrumental marks the means, company, or complement.
cases.translation: Natásha knew that she ought to go away, but was unable to do so: something gripped her throat, and regardless of manners she stared straight at Prince Andréy with wide-open eyes.

cases.sentence: — Да, — сказала графиня и протянула ему руку и с ___ отчужденности и нежности прижалась губами к его лбу, когда он наклонился над ее рукой.
cases.explain: «смешанным чувством» — after the preposition «с», the instrumental marks the means, company, or complement.
cases.translation: “Yes,” replied the countess. She held out her hand to him, and with a mixed feeling of estrangement and tenderness pressed her lips to his forehead as he stooped to kiss her hand. She wished to love him as a son, but felt that to her he was a stranger and a terrifying man. “I am sure my husband will consent,” said the countess, “but your father …”

cases.sentence: — Мой отец, которому я сообщил свои планы, ___ согласия положил то, чтобы свадьба была не раньше года.
cases.explain: «непременным условием» — the instrumental marks the means, company, or complement.
cases.translation: “My father, to whom I have told my plans, has made it an express condition of his consent that the wedding is not to take place for a year. And I wished to tell you of that,” said Prince Andréy.

cases.sentence: Наташа сидела на своей кровати, бледная, с ___, смотрела на образа и, быстро крестясь, шептала что-то.
cases.explain: «сухими глазами» — after the preposition «с», the instrumental marks the means, company, or complement.
cases.translation: “Lord have mercy upon us!” she repeated while seeking her daughter. Sónya said that Natásha was in her bedroom. Natásha was sitting on the bed, pale and dry-eyed, and was gazing at the icons and whispering something as she rapidly crossed herself. Seeing her mother she jumped up and flew to her.

cases.sentence: «Неужели этот ___ сделался теперь всё для меня?» спросила она себя и мгновенно ответила: «Да, всё: он один теперь дороже для меня всего на свете».
cases.explain: «чужой человек» — the subject of the sentence stands in the nominative.
cases.translation: Natásha never remembered how she entered the drawing room. When she came in and saw him she paused. “Is it possible that this stranger has now become everything to me?” she asked herself, and immediately answered, “Yes, everything! He alone is now dearer to me than everything in the world.” Prince Andréy came up to her with downcast eyes.

cases.sentence: — Да, да, — как будто с досадой проговорила Наташа, громко вздохнула, ___, чаще и чаще, и зарыдала.
cases.explain: «другой раз» — the accusative marks the direct object of the verb.
cases.translation: “Yes, yes!” Natásha murmured as if in vexation. Then she sighed loudly and, catching her breath more and more quickly, began to sob.

cases.sentence: — Вы знаете, что с того ___, как вы в первый раз приехали в Отрадное, я полюбила вас, — сказала она, твердо уверенная, что она говорила правду.
cases.explain: «самого дня» — after the preposition «с», the genitive here marks possession, absence, or quantity.
cases.translation: “Why do you say that?” Natásha interrupted him. “You know that from the very day you first came to Otrádnoe I have loved you,” she cried, quite convinced that she spoke the truth.
